case_name: McCorkill v. Streed, Executor of the Estate of Harry Robert McCorkill (aka McCorkell)
text:
S/M/49/13

IN THE COURT OF QUEEN’S
BENCH OF NEW BRUNSWICK

TRIAL DIVISION

JUDICIAL DISTRICT OF SAINT
JOHN

Citation:
McCorkill v. Streed, Executor of the Estate of Harry Robert                      McCorkill
(aka McCorkell), Deceased– 2013 NBQB 419

Date :          2013
11 13

BETWEEN:
ISABELLE
ROSE MCCORKILL

Applicant

-
and -

FRED
GENE STREED, EXECUTOR OF THE                                          ESTATE OF
HARRY ROBERT MCCORKILL                                         (AKA MCCORKELL),
DECEASED

Respondent

-and-

THE PROVINCE OF NEW BRUNSWICK as represented
by THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, THE CENTER FOR ISRAEL AND JEWISH AFFAIRS, LEAGUE FOR
HUMAN RIGHTS OF B’NAI BRITH CANADA, and THE CANADIAN ASSOCIATION FOR FREE
EXPRESSION

Interveners

BEFORE:                                    Justice
William T. Grant

HEARING HELD:                         Saint
John

DATES
OF HEARING:                  October 24
th
, November 5
th

& 13
th
, 2013

DATE OF DECISION:                   November
13, 2013

COUNSEL:

Marc-Antoine
Chiasson for the Applicant

John
D. Hughes for the Respondent

Richard
A. Williams for the Intervener, Province of New Brunswick as represented by the
Attorney-General

Danys
R.X. Delaquis for the Intervener, The Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs

Catherine
A. Fawcett for the Intervener, League for Human Rights of B’Nai Brith

Canada

Andy
Lodge for the Intervener, The Canadian Association for Free Expression

DECISION

GRANT, J

(Orally)

[
1
]     In
this motion, the Intervener, the Canadian Association for Free Expression
(CAFE) objects to the admissibility of certain paragraphs or portions thereof
in five affidavits that have been filed in support of this application by
Isabelle McCorkill for a declaration that the residual bequest in the last will
and testament of Harry Robert McCorkill is illegal and/or contrary to public
policy and that there is an intestacy in respect to the said residue which should
be distributed in accordance with the
Devolution of Estates Act
,
R.S.N.B. 1973 c.D-9.

[
2
]     Two of
the affidavits were filed by Ms. McCorkill, both of them sworn by Mark Potok, a
senior fellow at the Southern Poverty Law Centre in the United States.  The
third was sworn by Kevin Fornshill, chief executive officer and director of
Fringe Link Inc., a private company providing research and training for law
enforcement agencies and filed by the Intervener, the Province of New
Brunswick.  The fourth was sworn by Anita Bromberg, National Director of Legal
Affairs for the Intervener, The League of Human Rights of B’Nai Brith Canada.

[
3
]     The
fifth affidavit sworn by Shimon Koffler Fogel on behalf of the Intervener, The
Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs, is not going to be used on the
application so CAFE’s objections concerning it are moot.  CAFE requests costs
against the CIJA for not advising it that it would not be relying on the
affidavit on the hearing of the application but that request is denied because
I can find nothing on the Record on Motion to indicate that Mr. Koffler’s
affidavit, which was sworn July 26
th
, 2013 in support of its motion
for Intervener status in the application, would be relied upon in the
application.  CAFE apparently presumed that CIJA would be relying on it but
apparently did not call their lawyer to confirm that.  Neither did Mr.
Delaquis, the CIJA’s lawyer, call Mr. Lodge, CAFE’s lawyer, to advise him they
would not rely on it.  In my view, no costs award is warranted in favour of
either party in the circumstances.

[
4
]     CAFE
objects to the admissibility of the various portions of the affidavits for
failure to comply with Rule 39.01(5) which states:

(5)     An
affidavit for use on an application shall be confined to facts within the
personal knowledge of the deponent; but the affidavit may contain statements as
to the information and belief of the deponent with respect to facts which are
not contentious, if the source of his information and his belief therein are
specified in the affidavit.

[
5
]     In
summary, the affidavits must contain:

a)       facts
within the deponent’s personal knowledge; or

b)       statements
as to information and belief of the deponent                          concerning
non-contentious facts
provided
the source of the                        information
and belief is specified.

[
6
]     In the
case of
Charlebois v. New Brunswick

2002 NBQB 196
,
d’Entremont J. stated at paragraphs 14-15:

14.     The
requirements under Rule 39.01(5) are fundamental to the admission of the
allegations contained in an affidavit.  Information obtained from a third party
where the source of the information or belief is not identified is not
admissible.

15.
In
McDowell
v. Green
(1924),
1924 CanLII 716 (NB CA)
,
52 N.B.R. 114 (C.A.)
, Grimmer, J., explains at 117:

The well
known case of In Re J.L. Young Manufacturing Company Ltd.,
[1900] 2 Ch. 750

fully establishes the well recognized principle of law in matters of this
kind.  In that case the Court held that – an affidavit of information and
belief not stating the source of information or belief is irregular, and therefore
inadmissible in evidence, whether on an interlocutory or final application, and
a party or solicitor attempting to use such an affidavit will do so at his
peril as to costs.

[
7
]     Ms.
McCorkill has submitted two affidavits sworn by Mark Potok in support of her
application; one sworn on July 16, 2013 and the other sworn August 27, 2013.
CAFE objects to the admissibility of 10 of the 14 paragraphs of the July 16
th

affidavit and nine of the 13 paragraphs of the August 27
th

affidavit.

[
8
]     CAFE
submits that the affidavits contravene the restrictions set out in Rule
39.01(5) in that they contain opinion evidence, hearsay, excerpts of documents
taken out of context, argument and facts outside the personal knowledge of the
deponent which are contentious, not stated to be based on information and
belief and/or which do not specify the source of the deponent’s information and
belief.

MARK
POTOK’S AFFIDAVIT SWORN JULY 16, 2013

[
9
]     CAFE
submits that paragraphs 5-14 inclusive of Mr. Potok’s affidavit sworn July 16,
2013 are inadmissible.  Paragraph five reads as follows:

5.       Over the years at SPLC I have paid particular attention to
the National Alliance (NA), a neo-Nazi organization that has been one of the
most important and dangerous hate groups in America in recent years.  The SPLC
has gathered an immense amount of factual information about the group, which
was founded in 1974.  Since going to work at SPLC in 1997, I have become our
chief expert about the NA, writing dozens of articles, many of them in-depth
investigative pieces, on the organization, its members and their crimes.  I
have spoken to the media about the activities of the group and its members
hundreds of times.

[
10
]    CAFE
objects to Mr. Potok’s characterization of the NA as “a neo-Nazi organization
that had been one of the most important and dangerous hate groups in America in
recent years” as inadmissible in that it expresses his opinion and it purports
to state a fact which is clearly contentious.

[
11
]    The
grounds relied on by Ms. McCorkill in her amended application are set out at
paragraph five and they include the following at paragraph 5(g)(i) and (ii):

5(g)   The
payment or transfer of the residue of the estate           to the National
Alliance is against public policy and          in contradiction with Canada’s
own laws,           undertakings and commitments in that:

i.        The
National Alliance is a long-standing neo-             Nazi group in the United
States that has also                 been  active in Canada.  Through its hate                     propaganda,
the  National Alliance promotes a                     political program           parallel
to that of the original                   World War II-era  National Socialist
Party of               Germany (the Nazis)     including genocide,             ethnic
cleansing, and the use of hate                           motivated violence and
terror to achieve its               aims.

ii.       The
National Alliance has a long history of                  inspiring and carrying
out hate motivated            violence and terror through its members and                    supporters
in order to achieve its stated                     political aims.

[
12
]    In his
affidavit sworn July 26, 2013 in response to the application, Erich J. Gliebe,
the Chairman of the National Alliance, deposes at paras 6 & 7:

6.       Because
of the attention given to the NA in the affidavit of Mark Potok, I make this
affidavit chiefly in rebuttal of the characterizations therein of the NA as a
neo-Fascist organization and of alleged concerns with public policy.

7.       Throughout
my years in the NA, I have been aware of Mr. Potok’s writings for the Southern
Poverty Law Center (SPLC) and its publications, in particular because it has
depicted the NA as a “hate group”.  From this I believe the SPLC distorts the
facts and publishes false reports about the NA and its members.

[
13
]    The
grounds set out in Ms. McCorkill’s application must be proven by her in order
to satisfy this Court that the bequest is illegal and/or contrary to public
policy.  The two at paragraphs 5(g)(i) and (ii),
supra.
, form the basis
of the central issue which is before the Court in this application and they are
clearly contentious as can be seen from Mr. Gliebe’s affidavit.  The statement
by Mr. Potok at para. 5 of his affidavit of July 16, 2013 is essentially a
re-statement of those grounds.  At best, it expresses his opinion which is
inadmissible under Rule 39.01(5).  At worst, it states as a fact what is the
most contentious issue in this litigation and it is also inadmissible for that
reason.  It is therefore struck from this affidavit.

[
14
]    CAFE
also objects to Mr. Potok’s statement that he is the SPLC’s “chief expert about
the NA” as being an opinion.  Given that the statement merely establishes his
credentials within the organization, I find that it is more in the nature of a
fact within his personal knowledge and I will allow it.

[
15
]    In
paragraph six of his affidavit of July 16, 2013, Mr. Potok states:

6.       The
NA is dedicated to white supremacy, overthrow of the existing government and
the construction of a global “white living space.”  It is also explicitly
genocidal and violent in its ideology – a fact that the group does little to
hide.  In its foundational document, “What is the National Alliance?”, a copy
of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 1, the NA says:

“We will do
whatever is necessary to achieve this White living space and keep it White.  We
will not be deterred by the difficulty or temporary unpleasantness involved,
because we realize that it is absolutely necessary for our racial survival.”

[
16
]    This
paragraph clearly expresses conclusions from what is in the document attached
to it as Exhibit 1 and while the NA does not deny that the document has been
published by it, the first two sentences of the paragraph, which express those
conclusions, are inadmissible.

[
17
]    The
documents attached to Mr. Potok’s July 16
th
affidavit as Exhibits 1,
2 and 3 would be admissible since their authenticity has not been challenged by
the respondent but the sentence attaching Exhibit 1 begins an argument which
continues in paragraphs seven, eight and nine.  Consequently, I find the
remainder of paragraph six as well as all of seven, eight and nine are
inadmissible in their present form.

[
18
]    Paragraph 10 of Mr.
Potok’s affidavit of July 16, 2013 reads as follows:

10.     The
NA is explicitly Hitlerian.  In extensive writings and broadcasts through the
decades, the group has identified Jews as its chief enemy and spoken of the
“all-too-brief” period of Nazism in Germany, as it said in “What Is the
National Alliance?”  The cover of the March-April 1989 edition of
National
Vanguard
a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 4, then the group’s
main publication, was dedicated to the 100
th
birthday of Adolf
Hitler and featured a full-cover portrait of the Nazi leader.  Inside, in an
editorial by Pierce, it celebrated “the greatest man of our era – a man who
dared more and achieved more, who set his aim higher and climbed higher, who
felt more deeply and stirred the souls of those around him more mightily, who
was more closely attuned to the Life Force which permeates our cosmos and gives
it meaning and purpose, and did more to serve that Life Force, than any other
man of our times.”

[
19
]    The
first sentence of that paragraph expresses a conclusion in the nature of an
opinion and is therefore inadmissible.  The second sentence refers to an
exhibit which was attached at paragraph six which has been struck and will
therefore also be struck.  The remainder of paragraph 10 refers to an exhibit
which is admissible and states facts which are easily confirmed from the
exhibit itself.  It is therefore admissible.

[
20
]    Paragraph
11 of the affidavit states:

11.     The
scope of the NA has been remarkably international, especially in the years
leading up to Pierce’s death in 2002 (a successor, Erich Gliebe, has run the NA
since then).  Pierce foresaw an alliance of white supremacists around most of
the world, and he traveled frequently to Europe to try to build a “pan-Aryan”
movement.  He spoke to gatherings of the British National Party, then a
whites-only group, in 1995 and 1997.  He addressed a rally of the neofascist
German National Democratic Party (Nationaldemokratische Partei Deutschlandes,
or NPD) in 1998 and an NPD official addressed an NA conference the same year.
In 1998, Pierce attended a secret meeting of right-wing extremists in Greece,
according to the antifascist
Searchlight
magazine.  The following year,
he was back in Germany speaking to another NPD gathering.  In 2000, a neo-Nazi
child murderer wanted in Germany for violating his parole, who has been hiding
out at the NA headquarters compound in West Virginia, was arrested near the
compound and deported.  In 2001, two NPD officials joined an NA rally outside
the German embassy in Washington, D.C.

[
21
]    The
first sentence expresses an opinion and is therefore inadmissible.  The
remainder of the paragraph contains facts which are clearly not within Mr.
Potok’s personal knowledge without disclosing the source of his information or
stating that he believes them to be true.  The paragraph is therefore struck in
its entirety for failure to comply with Rule 39.01(5).

[
22
]    Paragraph
12 of Mr. Potok’s affidavit states:

12.     The
NA has long been active in Canada, as well.  In undated pamphlets from
www.natall.ca

(the NA’s former Canadian website), the group urged Canadians to “HANG CHILD
MOLESTERS!” a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 5 and to work for “A
Future for White Children” a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit 6.
“There will be no future for her,” that last pamphlet says below a photo of a
young white girl,  “in the Third World Canada that our nation’s enemies are
planning.  Let us take back our country and make it great, clean, decent and
beautiful once again.”  As of the early 2000s, the NA had contact points in
Calgary, Edmonton, Halifax, Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver (see Exhibit 7
attached hereto).

[
23
]    This
paragraph states a fact that is not disputed by the respondent and is therefore
non-contentious in my view.  It also attaches three exhibits to demonstrate the
source of the information.  I find that it is clearly admissible in this
application.

[
24
]    Paragraphs
13 and 14 read as follows:

13.     There is an extensive history of violence associated with NA
members and others who have been directly influenced by its propaganda,
especially
The Turner Diaries
, written by Pierce under a pseudonym.  The
book is a novel about a race war in which the FBI headquarters in Washington,
D.C., is bombed and white supremacists take over the United States.  It played
a key role in inspiring the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, the worst domestic
terrorist attack in U.S. history, and another infamous terrorist group:

•

December 1984:  Robert Mathews, the NA’s Pacific Northwest
organizer, is killed in a shootout with federal agents in Washington state
after launching a terrorist group informally known as the Order.  The name was
taken directly from the violent revolutionary group depicted in
The Turner
Diaries
.  Mathews’ group, formed in 1983, was behind the murder of a
prominent Jewish talk show host, armored car heists that netted $4.1 million,
and a series of other attacks.

•

April 1995:  Timothy McVeigh, patterning his attack closely on
the assault on the FBI building depicted in
The Turner Diaries
, blows up
a federal building in Oklahoma, killing 168 people.  When he was arrested,
McVeigh was carrying photocopied pages of the book in his car, apparently to
explain his motives in the event he were killed.  McVeigh is also known to have
called an NA recorded message line seven times the day before the bombing.

14.     The NA and its members have been linked to numerous other
major crimes and terrorist attacks.  Some examples:

•

A.  April 1997:  Alliance member Todd Vanbiber, who was slated
to attend an upcoming NA “leadership conference,” was badly injured when one of
14 pipe bombs he was building explodes in his face in an Orlando, Fla., storage
unit.  He later testified that he and three other men intended to use the bombs
as a diversion while they robbed banks in the greater Orlando area.  Vanbiber
and another man had earlier visited Pierce at NA headquarters and donated at
least $2,000 to the NA that they had garnered at an earlier bank robbery.
Vanbiber is sentenced to more than six years in prison.

•

B.  August 2000:  Carl Joe Carlson, a regional NA leader from
Nebraska, is charged after offering to deliver pipe bombs to what he thought
was a local militia group but was in fact a law enforcement trap.  He later
pleads guilty.

•

C.  June 2001:  NA member Eric D. Hanson is killed after a
14-hour gun battle and standoff with police in Lindenhurst, Illinois.  The
battle broke out when police tried to arrest Hanson, a convicted hate criminal,
for illegal weapons.

•

D.  October 2002:  NA member Samuel Compton was one of three
men who attached a bystander watching a bar fight in Phoenix.  Compton stomped
Cole Bailey, who was white, to death.  He was later sentenced to 22 years in
prison.

•

E.  March 2006:  NA member Jason McGhee and two other men
broke into a farmhouse in Cumming, Ga., and stabbed or shot four people to
death over an insult they suffered at the farmhouse earlier.  McGhee, who
prosecutors believe did all the killing, was given four consecutive life terms
plus 100 years.

•

F.  October 2010:  NA member Michael David Carrothers, who in
2008 had been named NA “Activist of the Year,” attacked a black man he had
never met with pepper spray in Columbus, Ga.  He was given a year in prison.

•

G.  January 2011:  NA member Kevin Harpham attempted to bomb a
Martin Luther King Jr. Day parade, in which more than 1,000 people were
marching, in Spokane, Wash.  The bomb was spotted and defused before
exploding.  Harpham was sentenced to 32 years in prison.

•

H.  August 2012:  Wade Michael Page, an NA supporter, murdered
six people at a Sikh temple in Oak Creek, Wisc., before killing himself.  Page
was a neo-Nazi musician who had played with, among other, Definite Hate, a band
that whose music was distributed by Resistance Records, the NA record label.

[
25
]    Erich
Gliebe addresses those paragraphs in his affidavit sworn July 26, 2013 as
follows:

12.     With regard to specific allegations about individuals,
Potok’s paragraphs 13 and 14, after consulting or reviewing such records as are
available to me, I can say that on that basis I believe McVeigh and Compton
were never members of the NA, that no records appeared for Vanbiber, Carlson
and Page, that Mathews left the NA in the 1980’s to form his own group, and that
Hanson was a member for a time.  Carrothers was dismissed after being
convicted, Harpham was dismissed for non-payment of dues six years before the
incident alleged, that McGhee left four years before the incident alleged.

[
26
]    The
respondent, Fred Streed, states at paragraphs 12 - 14 of his affidavit sworn
July 25, 2013:

12.     The affidavit of Mr. Potok on behalf of the Southern Poverty
Law Center I believe to be deliberately misleading, because the documentation
used is from the early years of the foundation and existence of the National
Alliance, Articles written by the founder Mr. Pierce more than a decade before
his death in 2002 are being advanced as a basis for invalidating the Testator’s
Will more than a decade after Pierce’s death.  A picture of Adolf Hitler is
clearly submitted for inflammatory, not probative, value.  To the extent that
the testator sympathized with the purposes of the National Alliance I believe
he was simply exercising his political freedom.

13.     It is also my belief that the political writings of the
founder of the National Alliance, William L. Pierce, were legal and in
compliance with the laws of the United States of America at the time they were
written.  As the laws and the social mores of the United States have changed with
time the message and views expressed by the organization have also changed.
These changes were advocated in no small part by the Testator, Harry Robert
McCorkill, before his death.  It is my belief that this is why Mr. Potok has
had to rely on material several decades out of date.

14.     The additional mention of specific individuals and their
crimes and punishment is a transparent attempt to smear the Testator and
Beneficiary with guilt by association, which I believe is not a legitimate
method of legal proof.  Since I am not affiliated with the National Alliance I
prefer to leave the particulars of these matters to the present head of the
National Alliance, Mr. Erich Gliebe, who has better access to the true facts of
membership alleged for those individuals in the affidavit of Mr. Potok than I
can command from my own recollections.

[
27
]    I note
firstly that neither the respondent nor Mr. Gliebe dispute the description by
Mr. Potok in paragraph 13 of
The Turner Diaries
including either
the substance of the book or its influence on NA members and others.  Neither
did they dispute that it played a key role in the Oklahoma City bombing.  Mr.
Potok offers these as facts within his personal knowledge and I accept that and
I find them admissible with the following exceptions which I find to be too
vague or speculative.

•

December 1984 … Mathews’ group, formed in 1983, was
behind

the murder of a prominent Jewish talk show host.

[
28
]    That
is speculative and does not make clear what he means by “behind the murder”. Then
he goes on to say:

•

… armored car heists that netted 4.1 million dollars and a
“series of other attacks”.

[
29
]    That
is too vague to have any probative value so I will strike that sentence from
the affidavit.

[
30
]    With
respect to the second “bullet” in paragraph 13, I will strike the underlined
portion of the following sentence:

When he
was arrested, McVeigh was carrying photocopied pages of the book in his car
apparently,
to explain his motives in the event he were killed.

as I do not
think that could be within his personal knowledge.

[
31
]    Mr.
Potok continues:

McVeigh is
also known to have called an NA recorded message line seven times the day
before the bombing.

He does not
give the source of that information so that sentence will also be stricken.

[
32
]    With respect
to paragraph 14, Mr. Gliebe confirms that four of the eight persons named
therein were at one time members of the NA and does not dispute the other
allegations.  Those paragraphs, being 14(c), (e), (f) and (g), are admitted.  The
remaining paragraphs 14(a), (b), (d) and (h) are struck as they are clearly
contentious.

MARK
POTOK’S AFFIDAVIT SWORN AUGUST 27, 2013

[
33
]    CAFE
submits that with respect to Mr. Potok’s affidavit of August 27, 2013,
paragraphs 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12, or portions of them are
inadmissible.

[
34
]    In
paragraph two, Mr. Potok deposes:

2.       In an earlier affidavit, I described the racist, genocidal
program of the National Alliance and detailed numerous violent crimes committed
by persons associated with the National Alliance or inspired by its program.  I
attached numerous exhibits to that affidavit to support my statements.

[
35
]    This
paragraph expresses opinion and while some of it is factual, the earlier
affidavit to which it refers is now somewhat different from what it was when
this affidavit was sworn.  Moreover, this paragraph is, at best, repetitive and
I therefore find it inadmissible.

[
36
]    Paragraph
four states:

4.       In his affidavit, Erich Gliebe, the National Alliance
chairman, does not contest the authenticity of Exhibits 1-6 attached to my
earlier affidavit.  Indeed, he refers to these exhibits as the “NA’s
foundational documents.”  But he contends that the documents are “decades old”
and do not reflect the National Alliance today.  Fred Streed makes a similar
claim in his affidavit.

[
37
]    CAFE
objects to this paragraph on the basis that it contains argument.  I disagree
and regard it as entirely factual and I allow it to stand.

[
38
]    Paragraph
six of Mr. Potok’s August 27
th
affidavit reads as follows:

6.       As I stated in paragraphs 6 and 7 of my earlier affidavit,
“What is the National Alliance?” sets out the Alliance’s goal of establishing a
“White living space” through a genocidal program of “racial cleansing.”

[
39
]    Since
paragraph six and seven of Mr. Potok’s earlier affidavit were struck, this
paragraph will be struck as well.

[
40
]    Paragraph
seven of Mr. Potok’s August 27th affidavit states:

7.       The June 2013 National Alliance homepage also advertised the
novel
Hunter
.  (Exhibit A.)  The novel, written by the National Alliance
founder, William Pierce, under the pseudonym Andrew Macdonald, depicts in
heroic terms the actions of a white nationalist who assassinates interracial
couples and civil rights figures.  The novel is dedicated to Joseph Paul
Franklin, a convicted racist serial killer currently on death row in the United
States, in these terms:  “Dedicated to Joseph Paul Franklin, the Lone Hunter,
who saw his duty as a White man and did what a responsible son of his race must
do, to the best of his ability and without regard for his personal
consequences.”  I attach hereto as Exhibit B the title and dedication pages of
the novel
Hunter
together with some excerpts which provide a clear
understanding of the nature and content of the novel.

[
41
]    CAFE
submits that this paragraph does not contain facts within Mr. Potok’s personal
knowledge.  I disagree.  The exhibits speak for themselves and their
authenticity is not challenged and they are therefore admissible.  If the
excerpts from the novel are out of context then the respondent can lead
evidence to demonstrate that and the Court can assess the evidence
accordingly.  I will strike as inadmissible the phrase in the second sentence,
“… in heroic terms”  as it is opinion.  Also, the deponent has not provided the
source for his characterization of Mr. Franklin as “a convicted racist serial
killer currently on death row in the United States” so I hereby strike those
words as well.

[
42
]    In
paragraph eight, Mr. Potok deposes:

8.       As late as at least April 2012, the National Alliance
website (see Exhibit C) also advertised
The Turner Diaries
, the race war
novel also written by Mr. Pierce, the National Alliance founder, that inspired
the murderous terrorist plots described in paragraph 13 of my earlier
affidavit.  I attach hereto as Exhibit D the title page of the novel
The
Turner Diaries
together with some excerpts which provide a clear
understanding the nature and content of the novel.

[
43
]    CAFE
submits that this paragraph contains opinion evidence and does not contain
facts within Mr. Potok’s personal knowledge.  I agree there are opinions which
must be struck but I am also satisfied that the paragraph contains facts within
Mr. Potok’s personal knowledge as confirmed by the exhibits, the authenticity
of which have not been challenged by the respondent.  In the first sentence, I
will strike the phrase, “the race war novel” as well as the clause, “that
inspired the murderous terrorist plots described in paragraph 13 of my earlier
affidavit.”  In the second sentence, I will strike the final clause, “which
provides a clear understanding of the nature and content of the novel” as both
are opinions.

[
44
]    In
paragraph nine, Mr. Potok deposes:

9.       Attached as Exhibit E to this affidavit is an April 2012
posting from a National Alliance website that highlights the issue of the
National Vanguard that paid tribute to Adolf Hitler on the 100
th

anniversary of his birth.  The cover of the issue – a portrait of Hitler – is
Exhibit 4 to my earlier affidavit and the accompanying article that describes
the leader of the Nazi regime as “the greatest man of our era” is quoted at
paragraph 10 of my earlier affidavit.

[
45
]    CAFE
submits that this paragraph also contains opinion and argument and that the
